title: Navigation and deep linking in SwiftUI
summary: Use `NavigationStack(path:)` where the path is an array of route values. Navigation becomes data: push = append, pop = removeLast, deep link = set the array.
body: **In simple words:** Instead of telling the screen "push this view", you keep an array like `[.product(id: 5), .reviews]`. SwiftUI shows the screens for whatever is in that array.

**Router (coordinator) object:** an `@Observable` class that owns the path and has methods like `showProduct(id:)`. Views call the router instead of knowing about other screens. This is the SwiftUI version of the Coordinator pattern.
**Deep links:** `.onOpenURL { url in router.handle(url) }` parses the URL into routes and sets the path. If the user is logged out, store the pending route and apply it after login.
**Sheets and full-screen covers** are separate state (`.sheet(item:)`). Include them in the router if deep links can open them.
**State restoration:** make routes `Codable` and save the path in `@SceneStorage`.
**Large apps:** each feature module registers its own destinations so the app shell does not import every screen.
keyPoints: A router/coordinator owns navigation state; views stay unaware of each other.
Deep link = parse URL → routes → assign path.

code.caption: Router-driven navigation

mistakes: Putting `NavigationLink(destination:)` everywhere so screens are tightly coupled.
followups: **Universal links vs custom URL schemes?** Universal links are https URLs verified by your domain; custom schemes can be claimed by any app.
**How do you test navigation?** Assert on the router's `path` array in unit tests.
